maria: hitting a weird combo of issues on Windows + Python 3.12 with the python SDK sample app. auth + ssl + typing/async all tangled. can anyone sanity-check?

maria: minimal repro (venv on Win10, python 3.12):

```
> pip install redwood-sdk certifi
> python sample_app.py

# sample_app.py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key=ENV["REDWOOD_KEY"])
await client.generate("hi")
```

Exception seen:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1007)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
redwood.errors.NetworkError: failed to establish TLS: certificate verify failed
```

Also get mypy failures for the async client types: `error: "AsyncClient" has no attribute "__aenter__"` when using `async with AsyncClient(...) as c:`.

devon: hmm. does this only happen on 3.12? works on 3.10/3.11? :eyes:

maria: 3.10 container is fine. 3.12 on local Win machine reproduces consistently. CI (linux) is green.

kevin: two separate things probably: 1) Windows+Py3.12 changed how the cert store is exposed to OpenSSL; sometimes `certifi` isn't picked up by the ssl module by default. 2) typing for async context manager sounds like our AsyncClient is missing the AsyncContextManager protocol.

lina: for the typing issue we had a similar complaint. mypy wants `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` definitions or to implement `typing.AsyncContextManager`. quick patch: in client/__init__.py add `class AsyncClient(AsyncContextManager["AsyncClient"]):` or implement `async def __aenter__(self): return self` and `async def __aexit__(self, *args): await self.aclose()` — that fixes mypy.

devon: for the SSL error try two quick workarounds: 1) set env var `SSL_CERT_FILE` to `python -m certifi` output, e.g. `set SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -m certifi)` (Windows: `for /f %i in ('python -m certifi') do set SSL_CERT_FILE=%i`) or 2) use `requests` style env var `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. also check if `python -m pip install --upgrade certifi` helps.

maria: tried `SSL_CERT_FILE` - still fails. `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` didn't change behavior. weirdly `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"` shows different paths on 3.12 vs 3.10.

kevin: if OpenSSL was built against the Windows cert store, Python may ignore certifi unless SSL_CERT_FILE is pointing directly at the PEM. can you paste `python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)"` output?

maria: `OpenSSL 3.0.11 22 Sep 2023`

kevin: ok. Next suggestion: as a short-term SDK change we can prefer `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())` when constructing TLS contexts in our HTTP transport on Windows. that makes the SDK more deterministic across platforms.

lina: agree. that change also won't break Linux/containers. we should gate it behind `platform.system() == "Windows" or os.environ.get('REDWOOD_FORCE_CERTIFI')` so folks can opt-in.

devon: also noted: when auth fails due to TLS we currently raise `NetworkError`, which obscures the underlying auth vs cert problem in some logs. propose adding a distinct `TLSError` subclass and surface the original `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError` in the exception chain. I'll open an issue.

ci-bot: CI run #4521: windows-integration-tests failed on test_sample_app (ssl verify) — see https://ci.internal/jobs/4521 (attached logs)

kevin: thanks @ci-bot. I'll cut a small PR with two changes: 1) prefer certifi PEM in transport creation on Windows, 2) add `async def __aenter__/__aexit__` shim in AsyncClient to satisfy typing. patch snippet:```python
# transport.py
import certifi, ssl, platform
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) if platform.system() == "Windows" else ssl.create_default_context()
# client.py
class AsyncClient:
    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self
    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        await self.aclose()
```
maria: if you can also preserve raising the original ssl exception in the chain that's huge. I can validate tomorrow. :pray:

lina: i'll review the typings bit. we should add unit tests for `mypy` in the SDK test matrix so this doesn't regress.

devon: opened issue #1287: "Windows/Python3.12 SSL cert verification + async typing edgecases" with steps to reproduce and logs. assigning to @kevin.

kevin: PR #1293 incoming, small change + tests. marking as draft until I validate on a Win 3.12 VM.

maria: awesome, thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. will follow up with logs after PR lands. :shipit:

kevin: will also add a short note in the devex docs about Windows cert pitfalls and how to set `SSL_CERT_FILE` on cmd/powershell.

maria: filing a sample-app attachment to the issue with my exact steps and a zipped venv (sanitized).
